vulkanmod.options.windowMode.tooltip: Controls how Minecraft uses the display. Exclusive fullscreen can reduce desktop-compositor overhead, while windowed fullscreen makes switching apps faster.
vulkanmod.options.resolution.tooltip: Sets the output resolution used in exclusive fullscreen. Higher resolutions look sharper but require more GPU work and video memory.
vulkanmod.options.refreshRate.tooltip: Sets the monitor refresh rate used in exclusive fullscreen. Higher rates can display more frames when the monitor and GPU can keep up.
vulkanmod.options.framerateLimit.tooltip: Caps how many frames Minecraft renders each second. A sensible cap reduces GPU load, heat, and power use and can make frame pacing steadier; Max removes the cap.
vulkanmod.options.vsync.tooltip: Synchronizes displayed frames with the monitor to prevent screen tearing. It may add input latency and limits FPS to the active refresh rate.
vulkanmod.options.guiScale.tooltip: Changes the size of menus, text, and the HUD without changing the 3D render resolution. Auto selects a scale for the current window size.
vulkanmod.options.gamma.tooltip: Adjusts scene brightness so dark areas are easier or harder to see. This has no meaningful performance cost.
vulkanmod.options.viewBobbing.tooltip: Moves the camera slightly while walking and sprinting. Disable it for a steadier view; performance is effectively unchanged.
vulkanmod.options.attackIndicator.toolti: Chooses where the melee attack-cooldown indicator appears, or hides it. This changes only the HUD.
vulkanmod.options.autosaveIndicator.tool: Shows an icon while the world is being saved. Disabling the icon does not disable autosaving or remove save-related pauses.
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.tool: Applies a coordinated group of graphics and VulkanMod settings. Potato favors speed, Balanced mixes quality and performance, Quality favors visuals, and changing an individual preset setting switches to Custom.
vulkanmod.options.advCulling.tooltip: Skips chunk sections hidden behind terrain. Aggressive removes the most work but may cause visible pop-in; Conservative is safer, and Off renders every section inside the camera view.
vulkanmod.options.ao.tooltip: Controls block-corner shading. Off uses flat lighting, On uses smooth lighting, and ON (Sub-block) improves shading on partial blocks with extra rebuild cost and experimental visuals.
vulkanmod.options.deviceSelector.tooltip: Selects the GPU VulkanMod uses. Auto is recommended; changing the device takes effect after restarting Minecraft. Current device: %s
vulkanmod.options.entityCulling.tooltip: Stops drawing entities in chunk sections that are not visible. This can greatly help in crowded areas and changes rendering only, not entity simulation.
vulkanmod.options.frameQueue.tooltip: Sets how many frames Vulkan may keep in flight. Higher values can keep the GPU busier and smooth some stalls, but use more memory and add input latency; 2 is the most responsive.
vulkanmod.options.indirectDraw.tooltip: Submits many terrain draws through fewer CPU calls. It usually helps when the CPU or driver is the bottleneck, but can add GPU or driver overhead and requires supported hardware.
vulkanmod.options.adaptiveChunkUploads.t: Smoothly adjusts chunk preparation and upload budgets using measured chunk cost and Vulkan backpressure after recent transfers. It ignores unrelated FPS drops, recovers gradually, and never exceeds the configured ceiling.
vulkanmod.options.chunkUploadsPerFrame.t: Sets the hard maximum number of completed chunk sections uploaded in one frame. Higher values reveal terrain faster but can create transfer or GPU-fence spikes; Adaptive mode may temporarily use fewer.
vulkanmod.options.renderDistance.tooltip: Controls how many chunks are drawn around the camera. Higher distances show more terrain but increase chunk building, CPU use, GPU load, and memory use.
vulkanmod.options.simulationDistance.too: Controls how far chunks keep ticking entities, redstone, and crops. In single-player this directly increases integrated-server CPU work; multiplayer is also limited by the server.
vulkanmod.options.prioritizeChunkUpdates: Controls how urgently visible chunk meshes are completed. Threaded gives smoother movement but may show terrain later; blocking modes reveal updates sooner and can cause larger frame stalls.
vulkanmod.options.graphics.tooltip: Controls Minecraft's main visual-quality effects. Fancy improves foliage and other effects; Fast reduces rendering work for higher FPS.
vulkanmod.options.particles.tooltip: Controls how many effect particles are created and drawn. Lower settings reduce CPU and GPU work during combat, weather, explosions, and busy farms.
vulkanmod.options.renderClouds.tooltip: Controls cloud rendering quality. Fancy clouds have more depth and cost more GPU time; Fast is cheaper, and Off removes cloud rendering.
vulkanmod.options.biomeBlendRadius.toolt: Blends grass, foliage, and water colors across nearby biomes. Larger areas make borders smoother but increase chunk rebuild time.
vulkanmod.options.entityShadows.tooltip: Draws simple shadows beneath entities. Disabling them provides a small GPU saving in areas with many mobs or players.
Scales how far entities remain visible. Higher percentages show distant entities but increase CPU and GPU work, especially in crowded scenes.
vulkanmod.options.mipmapLevels.tooltip: Creates lower-resolution texture copies for distant blocks. Higher levels reduce shimmering but use more video memory and require a texture reload when changed.
vulkanmod.options.uniqueOpaqueLayer.tool: Uses a dedicated combined layer for solid terrain to reduce render-state and draw overhead. Changing it rebuilds chunks and unusual shader or rendering mods may prefer it disabled.
vulkanmod.options.particleCulling.toolti: Skips redundant particles using distance, camera direction, and same-type limits. Quality is conservative, Balanced removes more, Performance is most aggressive, and Off draws every generated particle.
vulkanmod.options.blockEntityCulling.too: Stops drawing chests, signs, spawners, and other block entities when they are outside the camera view or too distant. Their game logic continues running normally.
vulkanmod.options.leavesCulling.tooltip: Removes hidden faces between adjacent leaf blocks, reducing forest geometry substantially. Transparent resource packs may make the visual difference more noticeable.
vulkanmod.options.textAntialiasing.toolt: Smooths font text so signs stay readable from far away or at an angle, and text from font packs looks clean. Applies immediately; uses slightly more video memory.
vulkanmod.options.textureAnimations.tool: Updates animated textures such as water, lava, fire, and portals. Disabling it makes those textures static and reduces animation-update work.
vulkanmod.options.renderScale.tooltip: Renders the 3D scene at a percentage of the window resolution, then scales it to the display. Lower values greatly reduce GPU load but make the world look softer; the interface stays readable.
vulkanmod.options.builderThreads.tooltip: Controls background chunk-building workers. Auto leaves CPU headroom for Minecraft and the integrated server; higher manual values can build chunks faster but compete with other work.
vulkanmod.options.backfaceCulling.toolti: Skips hidden block faces and culls the back side of opaque terrain. Disable only for models with incorrectly missing faces; disabling increases terrain geometry.
vulkanmod.options.wayland.tooltip: Forces GLFW's native Wayland backend on Linux when supported. Restart Minecraft after changing this option.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
vulkanmod.diagnostics.empty: Open Diagnostics to capture the current status.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.tooltip: Closes settings, counts down for three seconds, then measures ten seconds of normal gameplay.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.unavaila: Join a world before running the performance snapshot.
Apply or undo pending settings first.
A performance snapshot is already running.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.failed: Performance snapshot failed because too few frames were captured.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.stale.va: World context or settings changed since this run
vulkanmod.diagnostics.session.truncated: %s more entries omitted from this capture
vulkanmod.diagnostics.issue.mod_inventor: Loaded mod details could not be read
vulkanmod.diagnostics.flag.requested_una: Requested, but unavailable in this build
Confidence: %s | performance impact: %s | visual impact: %s | restart: %s
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.incomp: No VulkanMod setting can resolve another renderer replacement. Update or remove that renderer, or use it in a separate profile.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.mod_in: Refresh once. If the inventory still fails, copy the report and include it when reporting the problem.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.runtim: Investigate the suppressed mod or graphics failure
VulkanMod isolated a compatibility-call failure. Update the relevant mod and copy this report; settings cannot repair an exception or a failed graphics call.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.missin: Update the mod requesting unsupported graphics functions
A requested graphics function is missing or limited. Copy the report and update the mod; the troubleshooting baseline can only reduce other variables.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.gl_con: VulkanMod used a fallback for an incomplete graphics contract. Copy the report if the same scene has visual problems.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.versio: Update or roll back the listed mod to the verified version family. This warning does not change its runtime compatibility mode.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.unknow: The mod is recognized, but its version could not be verified. Check the installed file before troubleshooting rendering behavior.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.conser: Troubleshooting only: switch up to three rendering conditions to conservative values, retest the same scene, then use Undo before Apply if the preview is not acceptable. Restoring native render scale can substantially increase GPU work. This does not fix missing APIs.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.benchm: The current snapshot shows uneven frame pacing. Compare deliberate changes in the same scene; a short snapshot cannot prove a universal improvement.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.preview.sco: Stages settings only; mods, compatibility modes, and render-path ownership are unchanged
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.succe: %s change(s) staged. Use Apply to commit or Undo to discard.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.appli: Doctor changes applied. Run another snapshot in the same scene for comparison.
Doctor changes applied. No fresh before snapshot was available, so no comparison will be shown.
Doctor changes applied, but the world, window, or settings context changed before Apply. The saved baseline was discarded.
Settings changed after the Doctor preview. The changes were applied, but no comparison baseline was saved.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.draft: The staged settings no longer match the Doctor preview, so its comparison plan was discarded. Your remaining drafts are preserved.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.block: Apply or undo the existing staged settings before using this action.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.resul: Settings changed after the preview. Refresh Diagnostics and review the new plan.
Apply or undo the existing staged settings first.
A required setting is unavailable in this screen.
The proposed action was rejected by the safe-setting allowlist.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.n: Run a current-settings snapshot before staging Doctor changes to save a baseline.
No fresh baseline was available when these changes were staged.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.b: Fresh baseline saved; use Apply before running the after snapshot.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.a: Baseline saved. Run another snapshot after applying the staged changes.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.r: Comparable before and after snapshots are available.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.c: The world, dimension, or window context changed; these snapshots are not compared.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.s: Settings no longer match the confirmed Doctor plan; run a new baseline.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.i: A snapshot contains invalid or insufficient measurements.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.d: Short snapshots are directional; repeat them in the same scene. Differences under 2% and isolated long frames are treated as normal noise. The Doctor does not claim that a setting fixed compatibility.
vulkanmod.options.animateOnlyVisibleText: Animated textures (water, lava, fire, portals and modded blocks) update only while something on screen uses them, which saves client tick time. Turn off if an animation stays frozen.
vulkanmod.visuals.enabled.tooltip: The effects on the world below: lighting and shadows, sky, fog and clouds, water, bloom and colour (not the hand or the GUI). Off shows the game as before
vulkanmod.visuals.exposure.tooltip: Brightness of the scene before tone mapping
vulkanmod.visuals.tone_strength.tooltip: Film-like curve that rolls highlights off instead of clipping them. 0 keeps the colours as they are
vulkanmod.visuals.grade_strength.tooltip: Warms bright areas by the sun's height (orange at sunset) and cools dark ones. 0 leaves the colours as they are
vulkanmod.visuals.bloom_strength.tooltip: A soft glow mixed over the whole image, brightest around the sun, the sky and lights, and thicker with distance
vulkanmod.visuals.vignette_strength.tool: Darkens the corners of the screen
vulkanmod.visuals.fog_strength.tooltip: Haze over the distance and a ground fog over low land and water, thicker in rain and on calm mornings. 0 turns it off
vulkanmod.visuals.fog_height.tooltip: How quickly the fog thins with height above sea level
vulkanmod.visuals.weather_fog.tooltip: Rain and thunderstorms fade the distance into a blue-grey fog, as shader packs do. 0 keeps the clear-weather fog
vulkanmod.visuals.distance_haze.tooltip: The air's haze over the distance: a blue veil from a few blocks out that settles a few hundred blocks away, warm toward a low sun, and the far fade into the sky. Lower it for clearer far views
vulkanmod.visuals.sun_glow.tooltip: Warm light scattered in the fog toward the sun
vulkanmod.visuals.sunset_light.tooltip: Sunrise and sunset colour on the terrain
vulkanmod.visuals.light_shafts.tooltip: Sunbeams in the air. With Sun Shadows: volumetric light through the shadow maps wherever terrain or trees block the sun, thinner in rain; without: rays only while the sun is on screen
vulkanmod.visuals.moonlight.tooltip: At night: light on terrain under the open sky and the moon's light in the sky; caves stay dark. 0 adds no moonlight
vulkanmod.visuals.sun_shading.tooltip: By day under the open sky: faces turned from the sun get darker and short shadows fall next to walls and under trees
vulkanmod.visuals.ao_strength.tooltip: Darkens creases, corners and the ground under overhangs where light from the sky and the surroundings cannot reach; direct sunlight and torch light are not darkened
vulkanmod.visuals.water_depth.tooltip: Shallow water shows its bed, deeper water turns blue and darker, darker still at night
vulkanmod.visuals.water_reflections.tool: Calm water mirrors the sky, the land and ships, more strongly toward the horizon; ice reflects faintly
vulkanmod.visuals.block_reflections.tool: Polished stone, quartz, glazed terracotta, ice and gem blocks, and metal blocks: Highlights gives them the sun's and the moon's shine; Reflections also mirrors the sky and the scene on them, softly, metal in its own colour
vulkanmod.visuals.water_ripples.tooltip: Small texel-sized waves stir the water: its reflections, the sun's glints and the view below the surface; stronger in rain and storms, far water stays calm
vulkanmod.visuals.water_ripple_speed.too: How fast the ripples flow; 0 holds them still
vulkanmod.visuals.water_ripple_density.t: How close together the ripples are. 100 is the default; higher makes shorter, finer waves, lower makes long, smooth swells. The waves keep their steepness either way
How far you can see under water. 100 is the default; higher makes the water clearer, lower makes it murkier. Looking up, the surface shows the sky through a rippling window
vulkanmod.visuals.foliage_wind.tooltip: Grass, flowers and leaves sway in the wind, with the water ripples' speed (faster in rain); 0 holds them still
vulkanmod.visuals.far_clouds.tooltip: Draws the clouds out to the far view distance with rounded edges and shading, and mirrors them on water; off restores vanilla's clouds
vulkanmod.visuals.cloud_style.tooltip: Vanilla Shape keeps the far clouds in vanilla's blocky cells; Realistic draws billowing cumulus with rounded bases, shaded undersides and bright edges toward the sun, and thin cirrus streaks high above; Anime draws big soft puffy clouds with white tops and gentle blue-grey undersides, which thin out into the haze toward the horizon. The Anime colour palette picks Anime. Realistic and Anime cost more
vulkanmod.visuals.cloud_coverage.tooltip: How much the realistic clouds fill out: lower thins and shrinks every cloud at once, higher swells them until they merge (200 is nearly overcast, 0 clears the sky). Rain adds more. Size and Count change the clouds themselves, not how full they are
vulkanmod.visuals.cloud_size.tooltip: How big each realistic cloud is, and the gaps between them: higher gives fewer, larger and taller clouds over the same share of the sky, lower many small ones. Larger clouds cost a little more
vulkanmod.visuals.cloud_count.tooltip: How many realistic clouds there are: lower removes whole clouds and leaves the others as they are, so the sky clears in patches. 100 is the default; 200 keeps every cloud
vulkanmod.visuals.cloud_quality.tooltip: How finely the realistic clouds are traced: higher gives crisper edges and smoother shading at more cost
vulkanmod.visuals.celestial_shape.toolti: Square keeps vanilla's square sun and moon; Round draws a round sun with a softly darkened rim and a round moon that keeps its phases, in the sky and mirrored on calm water
vulkanmod.visuals.sun_size.tooltip: How big the round sun is. 100 is the default; a smaller sun is brighter, so its light shafts keep their strength. The square sun keeps vanilla's size
vulkanmod.visuals.moon_size.tooltip: How big the round moon is, with its maria and craters. 100 is the default. The square moon keeps vanilla's size
vulkanmod.visuals.aurora.tooltip: Curtains of green and violet light drifting across the sky: on clear nights in the Overworld (brightest in snowy biomes, never in rain or snow) and always in the End. Also seen in the water
vulkanmod.visuals.half_res_effects.toolt: Draws the shader rain and snow and the far clouds at half resolution and scales them up: much faster on weak GPUs (on integrated graphics rain costs about a quarter, realistic clouds about half), slightly softer (thin rain streaks, the edges of pixel-type raindrops). Auroras stay at full resolution. On in the Potato, Low and Medium presets. Off: full resolution
vulkanmod.visuals.aurora_strength.toolti: How bright the auroras are. 100 is the default; 200 doubles them
vulkanmod.visuals.star_type.tooltip: Vanilla keeps the square stars; Round draws each star as a soft round point of light (count, size, brightness and colour as set)
vulkanmod.visuals.star_count.tooltip: How many stars the night sky has. 100 is vanilla's sky; 0 has none, 400 four times as many (the stars of a lower count stay where they were)
vulkanmod.visuals.star_size.tooltip: How big each star is. 100 is vanilla's size
vulkanmod.visuals.star_brightness.toolti: How bright the stars are. 100 is vanilla's brightness, 200 twice the light. They still fade at dawn and dusk, in rain and behind clouds
vulkanmod.visuals.shader_weather.tooltip: Draws rain as thin streaks and snow as small drifting flakes in several layers of depth, with small splashes where it hits the ground, kept out from under roofs and caves, in place of vanilla's rain and snow columns and splash particles. Off draws vanilla's weather
vulkanmod.visuals.snow_type.tooltip: How the shader snow looks. Round draws soft round flakes that drift and blur with your motion; Pixel draws crisp pixel-art flakes in a few shapes, slowly turning; Both mixes the two, half each. Pixel and Both cost a little more while it snows (about 0.1 to 0.2 ms)
vulkanmod.visuals.snow_size.tooltip: How big the snowflakes are. 100 is the default
vulkanmod.visuals.snow_amount.tooltip: How many snowflakes fall. 100 is the default; more costs a little more while it snows (about 110% of the weather pass at 200, 75% at 50)
vulkanmod.visuals.snow_brightness.toolti: How bright the snowflakes are, apart from their colour (the Snow colour on the colours page). 100 is the default
vulkanmod.visuals.rain_type.tooltip: How the shader rain looks. Round draws thin soft streaks that stretch with the fall and your motion; Pixel draws crisp upright pixel-art drops of a fixed length; Both mixes the two, half of the drops each. Pixel and Both cost a little more while it rains (about 0.1 to 0.2 ms); the splashes on the ground stay the same
vulkanmod.visuals.rain_size.tooltip: How thick the raindrops are (and how long the pixel drops). 100 is the default
vulkanmod.visuals.rain_amount.tooltip: How many raindrops fall, and so how many splash on the ground. 100 is the default; thunderstorms add more; more costs a little more while it rains (about 110% of the weather pass at 200, 75% at 50)
vulkanmod.visuals.rain_brightness.toolti: How bright the raindrops and their splashes are, apart from their colour (the Rain colour on the colours page). 100 is the default
vulkanmod.visuals.sun_shadows.tooltip: Terrain casts shadows away from the sun, near and far (floating islands, mountains). Off: no sun shadows, faces are lit by their angle to the sun only
vulkanmod.visuals.vanilla_shadows.toolti: The near sun shadows also take the vanilla terrain around you: grass, flowers and leaves cast their own shape (with Sun Shadows)
vulkanmod.visuals.entity_shadows.tooltip: Mobs, players and dropped items within 32 blocks cast sun shadows (as whole model boxes); costs frame rate in crowds
vulkanmod.visuals.shadow_distance.toolti: How far around you the vanilla terrain casts sharp sun shadows; farther out the coarser far shadows (or the LOD shadows) take over. Each step costs frame rate when the sun moves
vulkanmod.visuals.sky_light_ambient.tool: Where the sun reaches, how much of vanilla's sky-light darkening is lifted (with Per-pixel Light); shade and caves keep vanilla's light
vulkanmod.visuals.per_pixel_light.toolti: Reads Minecraft's sky and block light per pixel: ravines keep their depth, cave water stops mirroring the sky; off uses the flattened lightmap
vulkanmod.visuals.light_colour.tooltip: Warm light where the sun reaches a face, cool sky light in the shade and blue moonlight at night (with the lighting pass). 0 leaves the colours as they were
vulkanmod.visuals.sun_warmth.tooltip: Colour temperature of direct sunlight: 100 is about 4000 K (the shade gets a little warmer too), 200 warmer still, 0 the sky's own white. Works through Light Colour
vulkanmod.visuals.block_light_colour.too: Warm orange light from torches and other light blocks, bright near the source and falling off faster. 0 keeps vanilla's colour and falloff
vulkanmod.visuals.block_glow.tooltip: Lava, magma, glowstone and other light blocks glow brighter, and the bloom spreads their light. 0 keeps vanilla's brightness
vulkanmod.visuals.ore_glow.tooltip: Nether quartz ore's white specks glow faintly, even in the dark. 0 leaves it like any other block
vulkanmod.visuals.held_light.tooltip: A torch, lantern, glowstone or lava bucket in your hand lights the blocks around you (with Per-pixel Light); walls stop it as they stop block light
vulkanmod.visuals.pbr.tooltip: Lights the terrain with the LabPBR maps of your resource packs (their _n normal and _s specular textures): bumps and grooves catch the sun, smooth and metal blocks shine and reflect, emissive texels glow, leaves let light through, and porous blocks such as sand or dirt darken in the rain while closed ones turn glossy. Needs Per-pixel Light and a LabPBR resource pack; without one nothing changes. Off: as before
vulkanmod.visuals.pbr_normal_strength.to: How deep the normal maps' bumps look: 100 is as the resource pack made them, 0 flat faces
vulkanmod.visuals.pbr_reflections.toolti: Smooth materials (polished, metal, wet) mirror the scene and the sky as rough or sharp as their smoothness; off keeps only the sun's and the moon's highlights on them
vulkanmod.visuals.pbr_parallax.tooltip: Textures with a height map look carved in depth up close (within about 20 blocks); off keeps them flat
vulkanmod.visuals.anti_aliasing.tooltip: SMAA on the final image (before the hand and the GUI): smooths jagged edges; higher presets search further along edges
vulkanmod.visuals.taa.tooltip: Temporal anti-aliasing: blends each pixel with the last frames along the camera's motion, which calms shimmering grass, leaves and shadows while turning; SMAA, when on, runs after it
vulkanmod.visuals.frame_generation.toolt: Shows a generated frame between the game's frames, made from the last frame's depth and the camera's motion: smoother turning without extra latency. Mobs and particles still move at the real frame rate. Turn it on when your frame rate is well below your monitor's refresh rate: it doubles the frames shown, and above that it only costs performance. Works best with vsync off on a variable-refresh display, or with Mailbox; the frame limit counts real frames.
vulkanmod.visuals.fsr_frame_generation.t: AMD FSR 3.1 frame generation: shows one generated frame between the game's real frames, and keeps the HUD sharp. Needs Windows and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3. Turns Optical Flow off. The frame limit counts real frames.
vulkanmod.visuals.fsr_frame_generation.u: Needs Windows: AMD's FSR library is Windows-only.
Needs a 64-bit x86 (x64) system: AMD's FSR library does not run on other processors.
Needs a GPU and driver with Vulkan 1.3.
AMD's FSR library could not be loaded; see the log.
The GPU has no spare queues for FSR's presentation.
The GPU lacks shader features FSR needs (storage image reads and writes without a format).
FSR stopped after an error this session; see the log.
vulkanmod.visuals.preset.tooltip: Sets the settings that cost GPU time at once: anti-aliasing, TAA, light shafts, clouds, auroras, shader weather, ambient occlusion, per-pixel light, sun shadows, water reflections. Settings that only change the look keep their values. Changing any of those settings shows Custom
vulkanmod.visuals.reset_defaults.tooltip: Shows every post-process setting at its default; Apply keeps them, Undo goes back
vulkanmod.visuals.light_debug.tooltip: Shows the per-pixel sky or block light in grey (red: not loaded yet), or the light colour's sun share, sky share and strength as red, green, blue, or what the water reflections mirror (magenta water, cyan ice and glass), or where each pixel's light came from (green the terrain light, blue the light volume, yellow the LODs, red not loaded yet); not saved
vulkanmod.visuals.block.frame_generation: Warning: frame generation costs GPU time, so the game renders fewer real frames than with it off, and above about 120 real fps it can show fewer frames in total. Use it when your frame rate is below your monitor's refresh rate. While either one runs, the game renders at most half your monitor's refresh rate (a lower frame limit in Video Settings still applies). Mobs, particles and the HUD still move at the real frame rate.
vulkanmod.visuals.block.materials.note: PBR needs a resource pack with LabPBR normal (_n) and specular (_s) maps; with none loaded these settings change nothing and cost nothing.
vulkanmod.visuals.title: Shaders
vulkanmod.visuals.edge_cover.tooltip: Covers the sides of built chunk sections that border sections not built yet, so no gaps show at the edge of the loaded terrain
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_preset.tooltip: Sets every colour on this page at once, with the bloom, saturation, fog and moonlight (how bright the night is) under it. Default: the look before the pickers. Realistic: after photographs of real skies and water. Cinematic: the teal-and-orange film look. Anime: a bright cel-shaded game look, with the Anime cloud style (another palette puts the clouds back). Horror: grey-green fog, a blood-red sunset and moon, almost dark nights. Changing any of them shows Custom. The performance presets never change these
vulkanmod.visuals.reset_colours.tooltip: Shows every colour on this page, and the bloom, saturation and fog, at its default (the Default palette); Apply keeps them, Undo goes back
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_day_sky.tooltip: The colour of the sky's light while the sun is high: the blue sky, its haze and the sunlit air. The sun and the clouds take it too. Click to pick; the default is the usual sky
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_sunset.tooltip: The colour of the sky's light while the sun sets in the west: the orange band at the horizon and the twilight dome above it
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_sunrise.tooltip: The colour of the sky's light while the sun rises in the east (by default a little cooler and paler than the sunset)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_sun_glow.toolti: The glow around the sun, on top of the sky's colour (Sun Glow on the Atmosphere page sets how strong it is)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_night_sky.toolt: The night sky's colour: the moonlit air and the faint glow of a moonless night
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_stars.tooltip: The stars' colour (white by default). A darker colour also dims them; their number, size and brightness are on the Atmosphere page
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_fog.tooltip: The ground fog and morning mist, the fog band at the horizon and the rain's fog; also the haze over nearby terrain, fading into the sky's own colour far away
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_overcast.toolti: The grey a rainy or stormy sky turns
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_clouds.tooltip: The far clouds' colour (both styles); they still take the sky's light
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_sunlight.toolti: The colour of direct sunlight on the ground and on blocks, and of shiny materials' highlights; it still warms toward sunset by itself (Light Colour on the Lighting page sets how much of it)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_shade_light.too: The colour of the sky's light on faces the sun does not reach: shadows and shaded sides by day (Light Colour on the Lighting page sets how much of it)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_moon.tooltip: The round moon and its reflection in water, and the colour of moonlight on the ground (Light Colour on the Lighting page sets how strong)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_block_light.too: The warm colour of torches and other light blocks, and of the glow of lava, glowstone and other glowing textures (Block Light Colour on the Lighting page sets how much of the light's colour)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_aurora_main.too: The main colour of the Overworld's auroras (green by default)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_aurora_upper.to: The colour high at the top of the Overworld's auroras (red-magenta by default)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_aurora_lower.to: The thin violet fringe at the bottom of bright Overworld auroras
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_aurora_end.tool: The colour of the End's auroras (all of its violet shades move with it)
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_water.tooltip: The colour deep water shows from above
vulkanmod.visuals.colour_underwater.tool: The water's colour around you when you are under water
vulkanmod.visuals.dh_lods.tooltip: Draws Distant Horizons' far terrain with the shaders' lighting, fog and shadows. Off draws no LODs; Distant Horizons keeps loading its data
vulkanmod.visuals.dh_shadows.tooltip: The far terrain from Distant Horizons also casts sun shadows (with Sun Shadows and Distant Horizons LODs)
vulkanmod.options.fpsOverlay.tooltip: Shows the frame rate in the top-left corner over the last 5 seconds. Simple: average FPS. Basic: average, min and max. Detailed: average, 1% low and 0.1% low (the frame rate of the slowest 1% and 0.1% of frames). Hidden while F3 is open.
vulkanmod.visuals.particle_smoke_type.to: Smoke from fires, campfires, explosions and ink. Vanilla keeps the pixel sprites; Realistic draws soft rolling puffs. Realistic costs a little more
vulkanmod.visuals.particle_smoke_size.to: How big each particle is. 100 is vanilla
How many particles each spawn makes. 100 is vanilla, 0 hides them. Only what you see changes (never the game). More costs a little CPU
vulkanmod.visuals.particle_smoke_brightn: Multiplies the brightness apart from the colour. 100 is vanilla. Glowing particles (flames, embers, end rods, portals) change their glow and bloom with it
The colour of smoke. The swatch is vanilla's typical colour; another moves every particle in the group by the same ratio (particles whose colour means something, like potions and redstone, stay apart)
